cues.en: All right.
In this section we are going to talk about sorting algorithms.
And here we are going to learn different types of sorting algorithms such as bubble sort selection sort
insertion sort, bucket sort, merge sort, quicksort and heapsort.
Now first let's learn what is sorting and why do we need it?
By definition, sorting refers to arranging data in a particular format, either ascending or descending.
It means we need sorting to sort given data either in ascending or descending order.
So let's see this example.
To make this definition more clear, here we have five different sized photos of this lady, and we
can see that the height of them are different and they are not in particular order.
Now if we apply any sorting techniques, the row will be like this.
And as you can see, they are standing in ascending order of their height.
Now you might be interested.
How do we arrange them in this order?
So for sorting we have different techniques as we are going to learn in our upcoming lectures.
So we can apply any of them to get this order.
Now the practical example of sorting can be Microsoft Excel.
So if you have ever used Excel, you might know that there is a built in function in Excel which is
used to sort data either in ascending or descending order.
By using this function, you can sort any given column's data in both ascending or descending order.
Similarly, if you search online shopping websites, they have sorting orders for their products.
On Amazon, for example, there are different criteria of sorting products that you want to buy.
So by using the sort option, you can sort products by price, reviews or rankings.
So these are the few real examples of sorting algorithms.
